newsitem.title: PERU: Japan says ransom report baseless.
newsitem.headline: Japan says ransom report baseless.

text.p: Japanese officials dismissed as baseless on Sunday a British newspaper report that Marxist rebels wanted a huge ransom to release some 340 hostages they hold at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

Britain's Independent newspaper reported on Sunday that the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) wanted several billion dollars from Japanese corporations whose executives are among the hostages.
Japan has a record in such crises of preferring to negotiate and pay rather than use force but a senior Japanese foreign ministry official said the London report was false.
"We haven't heard anything at all about demands for cash from companies involved, or anyone else," he told reporters.
The Japanese firms involved include Mitsubishi, NEC and Toyota, according to the Independent on Sunday.
"We have not received such demands here nor at headquarters in Japan," a senior Toyota representative in Lima told Reuters.
Other Japanese companies, including the other two mentioned by the newspaper, either had no comment or did not return telephone calls.

The newspaper claimed negotiations were going on between rebels and companies by cellular telephone. Reporters covering the story, however, say all cellular links in the area around the residence have been cut for days.
The rebel hostage-takers have complained repeatedly about their lack of telephone links to the outside world.
